Milo —

Here’s the sample you asked for: a redacted teardown in the format we’d use for a food & drink DTC launch.

Quick heads‑up: I couldn’t open sundriftdrinks.example, and warmcurrent.co returned a 502 for me. If there’s a different or staging URL, reply with it and I’ll run this against your actual page.

Sample excerpt (redacted)

1) Single‑offer page wireframe (one ad, one promise, one page)
- Hero repeats the ad’s promise; price/offer and primary CTA on the first screen.
- Proof: 2–3 small trust signals (press, early reviews, retailer logos if relevant).
- Product specifics: what it is, who it’s for, one visual that shows size/serve.
- Objections handled fast: short FAQ on taste, sweetness, alcohol %, shipping/returns.
- One action only (no top nav), sticky CTA on scroll.

2) How we run the first 90 days
- First two weeks are an audit: ad account, tracking, landing pages and the last 12 months of spend.
- Every ad concept ships in at least three variants so the account can learn which one works; we retire creative after about three weeks of falling click‑through.
- In later weeks we move budget to the concepts that keep winning.

3) First tests we’d run for drinks
- Offer: trial/variety pack vs bestseller bundle vs single‑flavour hero.
- Hook: taste/experience vs functional benefit vs social proof.
- Visuals: founder phone shot vs clean studio vs in‑hand/pour UGC. (For one client, a founder’s phone shot beat a £12k studio shoot in testing.)
- Format: six‑second cut vs 15‑second story vs statics.
- Page: short vs long; price‑first vs story‑first; FAQ placement.

Reference points
- Glow Theory: return on ad spend went from 1.6 to 3.1 over two 90‑day blocks.
- Oatside Kitchen: cost per first order down 38% after moving ads off the homepage onto three offer pages.

We work in 90‑day blocks, never longer contracts.
